issues.title: Plans-tab spawn/accept confirms default to Cancel, unlike the board's m/M confirm which defaults to Launch
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/move.go:240 (startFormOverriding, the board's m/M launch confirm) explicitly sets `m.binding = &formBinding{confirm: true}`, so a bare Enter on that confirm submits as the AFFIRMATIVE action (Launch) - confirmed live: pressing Enter on the board's kastest-freework go-confirm launched it immediately. By contrast cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:629 (startPlanSpawnForm, the plans-tab `m`-on-ready-plan spawn confirm) and plans_tab.go:420 (startPlanDoneForm, the project-UAT accept confirm) both build `b := &formBinding{}` with no `confirm: true` override, so the bound value defaults to false (Cancel) - confirmed live: pressing bare Enter on the plan-kastesthuge1 'Accept plan-kastesthuge1 and spawn 1 work item(s)?' confirm silently cancelled (status line read 'cancelled', zero launch) even though the visual layout looks identical to the board's confirm ('Spawn     Cancel', 'enter submit'). The existing unit test suite corroborates this is a real, load-bearing default: cli/internal/tui/plans_view_test.go:606, plans_view_test.go:674 and plans_tab_cross_project_skip_test.go:55 all have to manually override `m.binding = &formBinding{confirm: true}` after opening a plans-tab confirm specifically to simulate the affirmative path, i.e. the test authors already had to work around the same false default. A user whose muscle memory comes from the board (bare Enter = go) gets a different, silent-ish outcome on the plans tab purely from which form constructor they hit. The `y`/`n` shortcuts work fine as a reliable escape hatch (used throughout this round's hands-on drive once the pattern was understood), so this is not a functional blocker, but it is a real inconsistency in exactly the class of UX this plan is about (every outcome should be unsurprising, not just diagnosable after the fact).
issues.proposed_solution: In cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go, change `b := &formBinding{}` to `b := &formBinding{confirm: true}` at both startPlanSpawnForm (line 629) and startPlanDoneForm (line 420), matching move.go's startFormOverriding. Re-run/adjust the three tests that currently override this manually (plans_view_test.go:606,674 and plans_tab_cross_project_skip_test.go:55) - they should still pass unchanged (or become simpler, since the override becomes redundant) once the default matches. This is pre-existing behaviour from the 0.25.0 plans-board work, not introduced by this round's changes, so it may be a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight - the implement agent's call whether to fold it into this round or file it separately.
issues.fix_summary: Seeded `confirm: true` at both plans-tab confirm constructors - startPlanDoneForm (project-UAT accept) and startPlanSpawnForm (the `m`-on-ready spawn) - so the affirmative starts highlighted and a bare Enter submits, matching move.go's startFormOverriding. The user's decision: "m -> enter should confirm". Deliberately NOT changed: startDeleteForm (delete.go) and startKillForm (update.go) keep their explicit `confirm: false`, because a destructive/irreversible action must stay safe on Enter. Wrote the rule down as a named CONFIRM-DEFAULT CONVENTION: the canonical statement now lives in move.go's startFormOverriding (forward pipeline move -> true -> Enter submits; destructive -> false -> Enter is safe; the asymmetry IS the rule, never align the two families), with a pointer comment at each of the four other sites so the next person cannot 'helpfully' flip them. New confirm_default_test.go asserts BOTH halves by driving a BARE ENTER through the real huh lifecycle (keyPress pumps the async NextField/nextGroup/StateCompleted chain) and checking the real side effect: board `m` launches, plans-tab `m` spawns (launcher fires once, plan flips active with 1 member), plans-tab `m` accepts the project-UAT (plan flips done), while a bare Enter on delete leaves the feature on disk and out of trash and a bare Enter on kill calls the killer zero times. A third structural test derives each confirm constructor's seeded default from the source and fails on an UNSEEDED `&formBinding{}` - the exact shape that caused this issue. Mutation-verified with compile-check-first: 6/6 reverts fail, each in the expected test (both seeds, the board reference, both destructive defaults, and the fixture). Also fixed two round-02 test fixtures found while here: TestProjectUATRefusalIsBlocked and TestFinishPlanDoneRefusalIsBlocked omitted the member features' `Correlations`, so memberFeature never resolved them and both refused because the member was NOT FOUND rather than not shipped - a weaker reason than intended; the fixtures now carry the plan id and the refusal asserts the exact 1-of-2 tally.
